title: 6973GH-26-Q-00131 ASR-9 Beacon Cable Kits
description: 1. BACKGROUND The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has identified a requirement to procure conversion kits to support modifications to the Air Traffic Control Beacon Interrogator (ATCBI-5) configuration at Airport Surveillance Radar Model 9 (ASR-9) facilities as part of the Brand-New Air Traffic Control System (BNATCS) implementation under the Radar System Replacement (RSR) Program. The rotary joints currently installed at ASR-9/ATCBI-5 sites do not provide the number of signal paths required to support integration with the RSR architecture. To achieve compatibility, the existing rotary joints must be converted to the configuration utilized at ASR-9 sites equipped with the Mode Select Beacon System (Mode-S). This conversion requires the installation of a kit developed by AJW-1433, which replaces the existing beacon cables. 2. CONTRACTING OFFICER�S REPRESENTATIVE (COR): The COR formally designated this responsibility by the Contracting Officer to provide direction and Government oversight to the contractor on matters related to this contract. The COR is: Brandon Brumley AJW-L910, Radar Technical and Program Support Branch 3. SCOPE OF WORK The contractor must furnish all labor, facilities, equipment, and materials to fabricate a kit as outlined in each section that follows. A. CLIN 001 � One (1) First Article Unit - Shall be delivered 90 days After Receipt of Order B. CLIN 002 � Option to purchase up to nineteen (19) Production Units after first article approval 4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Design, Construction, and Testing The contractor shall procure and package the parts listed in Attachment 1 � Parts List into a Kit. 4.2 First Article Unit Delivery Contractor must deliver one verification unit. Delivery shall occur no later than (NLT) ninety (90) days at receipt of order (ARO). 4.3 Verification Unit Analysis Upon receipt of first article unit, FAA shall perform visual inspection to determine conformance to Attachment 1 � Parts List. FAA will have 30 days to accept or reject first articles. 4.4 Production Units Once approval is provided for the first article unit, the contractor shall be considered an approved source of production units. The number of units for production is nineteen (19). Delivery of production units shall occur NLT 180 days after notification of First Article Approval. 5. PREPARATION FOR DELIVERY 5.1 Preservation, Packaging, and Packing Preservation, packaging, and packing shall be IAW Provision 61.

title: 7A21--NRM| 460-24-009 CLC and Fourth Floor Patient Elopement Upgrade | NCO 4 Construction East (VA-26-00050011)
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government is seeking capability statements from commercial sources to determine market availability, technical feasibility, and potential small business set-aside avenues (SDVOSB) for an Enterprise Patient Elopement & Wander Management System. Please submit the following: Interested contractors shall submit a Capability Statement detailing: Company Information: Legal Business Name, SAM.gov UEI/CAGE Code, Point of Contact, and Socioeconomic Status under NAICS 541519. Technical Capability: Brief narrative demonstrating capability to deliver, install, and service an enterprise patient elopement platform. Indicate if providing brand-name products (e.g., GuardRFID, Stanley Healthcare/Huggies/WanderGuard) or equal custom solutions. Contract Vehicles: List any existing GWAC or FSS contracts (e.g., GSA MAS, VA FSS, SEWP) your firm currently holds that cover these supplies/services. 4. Response Guidelines Response Deadline: 9/11/26 3:00 p.m. Submission Format: PDF via email to cheryl.roberts2@va.gov Subject Line: Sources Sought Response - Patient Elopement System - [Company Name] Note: The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this notice. Statement of Need: Patient Elopement Prevention System, Wilmington VA Medical Center, Wilmington Delaware Background: Patient elopement represents a significant safety risk within healthcare facilities, particularly for vulnerable populations such as those with cognitive impairment, mental health conditions, or those at risk of harm to themselves or others. Elopement incidents can result in emotional distress, bodily harm, or even fatalities, and place a legal and reputational burden on the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). Need Statement: The VA Wilmington VAMC requires a comprehensive Patient Elopement Prevention System to proactively mitigate the risk of unauthorized patient departures ( elopements ), ensure the safety of patients, and comply with The Joint Commission and other regulatory requirements related to patient monitoring, safety, and reporting. Objectives: Prevention: Reduce the incidence of patient elopement from inpatient and specialty care units. Real-time Monitoring: Enable real-time location tracking and immediate alerts to staff if a patient at risk attempts to exit designated safe zones. Rapid Response: Provide timely notification to appropriate response personnel to intervene and prevent patient harm. Audit and Reporting: Facilitate post-incident reviews, trend analysis, and meet documentation/internal audit requirements. Scope: The anticipated system shall include, but not be limited to: Removal and proper disposal of the existing patient elopement prevention system and associated hardware in accordance with VA environmental and information security policies Installation and deployment of the new patient elopement prevention system Wearable tags or wristbands for at-risk patients Fixed and/or portable monitoring devices covering all potential exit points Integration with existing VA IT and security infrastructure Real-time notification to nursing stations and mobile devices Secure logging and reporting features Staff training and maintenance support Conclusion: The implementation of a Patient Elopement Prevention System will enhance the standard of care at Wilmington VAMC, protect Veteran patients, and ensure regulatory compliance. Procuring this system is essential to upholding the VA mission of providing safe, high-quality healthcare.

title: Tactical Air Traffic Control (ATC) Command and Control (C2) System (TACOS)
description: AMENDMENT 2 Posted on 20 August 2026. Responses to Questions submitted to the Government have been added to the attachments section. The response deadline is extended to 11 September 2026. Anyone who has already submitted a response and would like to submit an amended response based on the Q&As is welcome to do so. AMENDMENT 1 Posted on 24 July 2026. Revisions made to Paragraphs 2.4 and 2.8. 1.0 Description This is a Request for Information (RFI) only, issued as part of market research in accordance with (IAW) Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 10. This is not a solicitation/Request for Proposal (RFP), a Request for Quotation (RFQ), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), or a solicitation, and no contract shall be resultant from this synopsis. Aerospace Management Systems Division (AFLCMC/ESA) will not pay respondents for information provided in response to this RFI. Participation is limited to contractors registered in the United States. Submissions from non-U.S. contractors will not be considered. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center's (AFLCMC) Electronic Systems Directorate, Aerospace Management Systems Division (ESA), Air Traffic Systems Branch (ESAA) Program Management Office (PMO), located at Hanscom Air Force Base (AFB), Massachusetts, is requesting information from industry to assist in planning for the potential future acquisition of a Tactical Air Traffic Control (ATC) Command and Control (C2) System, hereafter referred to as TACOS. Current USAF expeditionary ATC systems were designed for a more permissive operational environment and are ill-suited for modern, multi-domain warfare. Legacy systems are characterized by large size, weight, power, and personnel (SWaP-P) footprints; prolonged setup and teardown timelines; limited interoperability with joint and coalition C2 systems, tactical data links (TDLs), and modern sensor networks; and susceptibility to kinetic and non-kinetic threats, including electronic attack, cyber intrusion, and electromagnetic pulse (EMP). These limitations create unacceptable risk to air operations under the pacing challenge and the requirement to project airpower from dispersed, austere locations. TACOS is envisioned as a critical enabler of the Department of the Air Force (DAF) Battle Network, providing the essential link between aircrew and the airfield environment across the full spectrum of operational environments � from permissive airspace to highly contested, denied areas of operation. TACOS shall be a modular, scalable, and highly interoperable system that ingests and processes tactical data feeds from Battle Management Command and Control (BMC2), Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), and Weather (WX) networks, fusing them with traditional Air Traffic Control (ATC) processing to display a unified airspace awareness picture. This provides commanders the flexibility to tailor Airfield Operations (AO) ATC services to the specific warfighting mission and threat levels. Core attributes include agility and speed (rapid deployment, minimal airlift, setup and teardown by a small team in hours); survivability and resilience (operation through kinetic and non-kinetic attack, low probability of detection, and function in a communications-degraded or -denied environment); seamless interoperability across USAF, joint, and coalition sensors and C2 networks; and scalable mission command. The operational requirement for TACOS is sponsored by Headquarters Air Force Flight Standards Agency (HQ AFFSA), the USAF lead agency for air traffic control, airfield management, and air traffic control and landing systems (ATCALS); acquisition is executed by AFLCMC/ESAA. The information received will be used to inform the development of a potential future acquisition strategy. Solutions should be actionable within the next two (2) years. This RFI does not commit the Government to any contractual agreement. 2.0 Key System Capabilities The desired TACOS solution must deliver an integrated, scalable suite of capabilities as a survivable, expeditionary, and interoperable C2 platform providing reliable ATC services in support of Agile Combat Employment (ACE). The system shall provide, at minimum, the following capabilities: 2.1 Expeditionary, Modular, and Mobile Design The TACOS architecture shall be non-proprietary and adhere to a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) governed by a Government-owned system architecture, enabling rapid integration of third-party hardware and software while remaining sensor-agnostic across current and future data sources. Open, consensus-based standards shall govern the large majority of Government-defined Key Interfaces so that hardware and software can be decoupled, and cloud-ready software containers shall allow individual capability modules (including Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) decision aids) to be upgraded, replaced, or added without disturbing the rest of the system. The solution shall be lightweight, compact, and ruggedized for sustained operation in austere, expeditionary environments, and rapidly deployable and reconfigurable to satisfy the personnel, setup-time, and logistical-footprint demands of each operational configuration. The system shall be inherently scalable, spanning both hardware and software, to support demand-varying configurations that range from a Low-Demand, single-operator, dismounted, man-portable setup to a High-Demand, multi-operator, shelter-based system, allowing commanders to delegate and optimize the configuration to mission need. Workstation capacity shall scale from a baseline of a few controller positions to several, and the equipment shall support rack-mount, pole-mount, and tabletop installations within an ATC tower as well as Mobile Tower, Landing Zone, and contingency-control roles. The system shall remain operable across the full spectrum of operating environments�from permissive airspace to contested and denied areas, and from austere landing zones to established main operating bases�without degradation of core ATC and C2 functions. Additionally, the system shall install within existing military or commercial structures and standard fixed and expedient shelters. The system shall reflect a self-contained, transit-case architecture designed for a tightly bounded expeditionary envelope. When fully deployed, the system shall operate within a 20-by-20-foot footprint. For mobility, the entire system shall be transportable on a single 463L pallet for airlift, via rail, or by a single light tactical vehicle, while remaining ruggedized to survive standard transit shock and vibration stresses. To facilitate rapid tactical movement, individual transit cases shall remain within two-person lift limits. A trained crew of no more than four personnel shall be capable of rapidly deploying and retrograding the system. To sustain operations away from fixed infrastructure, the system shall accept a wide range of Alternating Current (AC) and Direct Current (DC) power inputs, including Government-Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) generators, commercial grids, vehicle/aircraft power, solar arrays, and scavenged DC sources. The system shall automatically sense commercial power loss and transfer to organic generation without interrupting critical C2/ATC functions. 2.2 Integrated Data Fusion Engine TACOS shall operate as a sensor-agnostic, Multi-Level Secure (MLS) data fusion engine that ingests, correlates, and fuses inputs from organic and non-organic sources into a single, unambiguous track per object and a low-latency Single Integrated Air Picture (SIAP). Source data shall include Primary and Secondary Surveillance Radar (PSR/SSR), ADS-B, Mode S and Mode 5 Identification Friend or Foe (IFF), Tactical Data Links (TDLs) such as Link 16 via JREAP, Counter Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) tracks, and meteorological feeds, delivered in standard ATC formats including ASTERIX and Common Digitizer Model 2 (CD-2). title: 6973GH-26-Q-00130 - ASR-8 Weather Kits
description: 1. BACKGROUND The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has identified a requirement to procure conversion kits to support modifications to the Air Traffic Control Beacon Interrogator (ATCBI-5) configuration at Airport Surveillance Radar Model 8 (ASR-8) facilities as part of the Brand-New Air Traffic Control System (BNATCS) implementation under the Radar System Replacement (RSR) Program. The rotary joints currently installed at ASR-8/ATCBI-5 sites do not provide the number of signal paths required to support integration with the RSR architecture. To achieve compatibility, the existing rotary joints must be converted to the configuration utilized at ASR-8 sites equipped with the Mode Select Beacon System (Mode-S). This conversion requires the installation of a kit developed by AJW-1433, which adds an additional signal path to accommodate Weather Signal transmission through the rotary joint. 2. title: Ablation Laser
description: This is a Notice of Proposed Contract Action under RFO Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. This notice is for information only; a solicitation will not be issued. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION. No contract will be awarded on the basis of offers received in response to this notice. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 334413 (Semiconductor and Related Device Manufacturing) with a small business size standard of 1,250 employees. The Government requires the procurement of an Ablation Laser, and intends to negotiate a sole-source award for this requirement with RPMC Lasers, Inc. 8495 Veterans Memorial Parkway, O Fallon, Missouri, 63366-3085, who represents itself as the exclusive North American distributor of Quantum Light Instruments branded products (required brand name). Relevant part numbers and associated product descriptions are as follows: Item 1, qty. 1 each � Part #: Q1-C10-1064 16 mJ @ 10Hz @ 1064 nm, E-O Q-switching Item 2, qty. 1 each � Part #: Q1-H1-SH Stand-alone harmonics module, two output ports, 2nd and fundamental Item 3, qty. 1 each � Part #: Q1-AT2 Attachable module for 2nd harmonic attenuation (for single wavelength only) The Government has determined that other companies' products and services do not meet or cannot be modified to meet the Government's needs. Previously, in June 2026, the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) awarded a contract to RPMC Lasers, Inc. for the purchase of a very similar Quantum Light Instruments branded Ablation Laser to that currently being purchased. The currently required laser is intended to be integrated into existing testing infrastructure, which will include the previously purchased Quantum Light Instruments branded Ablation Laser. In order to maximize uniformity throughout the testing infrastructure, for standardization purposes, and to ensure compatibility and interoperability, the new Ablation Laser must also be Quantum Light Instruments branded as the existing one is. Considering this, and also considering interchanges with RPMC Lasers, Inc. yielded that they are the exclusive North American distributor of Quantum Light Instruments branded products, a sole-source award to RPMC Lasers, Inc. is contemplated, as aforementioned. This is a notice of proposed contract action and not a request for competitive proposals; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement or proposal, which shall be considered by the agency. All inquiries should be sent by email to Tabitha.Haggart@us.af.mil. Responses must be submitted by the date/time listed on the notice. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government in future procurements. Responses received will be evaluated; however a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government anticipates an award on or before 30 September 2026. A Sole Source Justification will be attached to the subsequent Notice of Award in accordance with applicable regulation.

This is a commercial supply acquisition in accordance with FAR Part 12 and FAR Part 13. The Contractor shall provide backflow preventers and service kits. The system should be certified to prevent contamination and require limited manual intervention and can be safely operated to minimize the impact on residence. The Contractor shall provide and deliver the following items : 14 Double-Check Valve Assembly (DCVA) Backflow Preventers with Installation Kit 2 x 1.5" Lead Free Double Check Valve Assembly 2 x 2" Lead Free Double Check Valve Assembly 2 x 2.5" Lead Free Double Check Valve Assembly with service kit 6 x 3" Lead Free Double Check Valve Assembly 4 x Service Kit for 3" Lead Free Double Check Valve Assembly 2 x 4" Lead Free Double Check Valve Assembly with service kit 1 x 6" Lead Free Reduce Pressure Zone Backflow Prevention Assembly with service kit All specialized tools, and instructions required to complete installation All certificates of applicable standards and codes All calibration and commissioning instructions The Government reserves the right to reject non-conforming products. 1. Mandatory Standards and Compliance ASSE 1015/CSA B64.5/cUPC: The device must meet these standards for double check valve assemblies. AWWA C510: Compliant with American Water Works Association standards for double check valve assemblies. NSF/ANSI/CAN 61 & 372: Must meet lead-free requirements and safe drinking water standards. Hazard Rating: Suitable only for non-health hazard (low hazard) applications. 2. Specifications (Technical Data) Assembly Components: Must be factory assembled, including two check valves, two shutoff valves, and four test cocks. Working Pressure: Minimum 175 psi (12.1 bar). Temperature Range: 33�F to 180�F (0.5�C to 82�C). Check Valve Type: Spring-loaded check valves. Sizes: 3/4" to 2" bronze bodies, 2-1/2" to 10" epoxy-coated iron. Shutoff Valves: Full-port resilient-seated ball valves (for sizes 2" and smaller) or non-rising stem gate valves (for sizes 2-1/2" and larger). Replaceable stainless steel seats Max Flow at low pressure drops Ease of maintenance Corrosion resistance of internals No special tools required for servicing Captured spring assemblies for safety 3. Common Recommended Models Watts: Series LF007 (Lead Free) or Series 757. FEBCO: Series 850 Small (Lead Free). Ames Fire & Waterworks: Series 2000B (Small) or 2000SS All items must be supplied with a mimum Warranty of 1 year Delivery Terms Delivery shall be no more than 30 calendar days after award, FOB Destination - SUVI Global Services - Doral, FL. 33178. US. The Contractor shall be responsible for all costs associated with packaging, handling, transportation and delivery. The items should be packaged for international shipping to final destination - US Embassy Kingston - Kingston, Jamaica Response Quotations should be sent in USD excluding duties or taxes and must include delivery time, warranty information, detailed product specifications and certification documentation . All firms that respond to this request for quotation must at the time of submitting their quotations must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). Interested parties should email quotations with completed NDAA889 representations to kingstonquotes@state.gov no later than the response date.

title: Operate Refuse Transfer Station, Collection/Disposal of Refuse and Recycling Contract
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice does NOT constitute a request for proposal, request for quote, or invitation for bid. There will not be a solicitation, specifications, or drawings available at this time. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this synopsis or any follow-up information requests. This is a sources sought synopsis announcement to obtain market survey information to be used for preliminary planning purposes in order to facilitate with the acquisition planning decision-making process. The intent of this notice is to identify potential offerors and to determine whether to set-aside the requirement for small business concerns in the upcoming solicitation. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Mid-Atlantic, Facilities Engineering, Acquisition, and Design Cherry Point, is specifically seeking certified 8(a) Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses, Women Owned Small Businesses, Economically Disadvantaged Women Owned Small Businesses, or other Small Businesses with current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capabilities to perform the proposed requirement. The successful Contractor shall be required to provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, material, and equipment required to sort and accept refuse, recycling, painted and treated wood debris at the refuse transfer station, along with the collection of refuse and recycling from various locations from Contractor provided dumpsters. The refuse transfer station normal working hours are Monday through Friday excluding federal holidays between the hours of 7:00 am to 3:30 pm. The Contractor is responsible for the weekly disposal of all refuse from the designated collection point. This service includes the removal of miscellaneous unpainted wood and contaminated debris, such as metal and construction materials. However, it expressly excludes white goods (e.g., appliances), brown goods (e.g., furniture), tires, and batteries. To complete these tasks, the Contractor must provide all necessary equipment, including a frontend loader and tractor-trailers. All work must be performed in strict compliance with the most current federal, state, regional, and local laws, ordinances, and regulations governing refuse transfer and disposal. The Contractor is also required to implement robust quality controls and review procedures to prevent conflicts, errors, and omissions. A combination firm-fixed price/indefinite quantity indefinite delivery (IDIQ) contract type, utilizing performance-based specifications, with recurring and non-recurring services is anticipated. The IDIQ work may be ordered utilizing FEDMALL or on a task order basis. The order will specify the exact location and types of work to be accomplished. The total contract term, including the exercise of any options, shall not exceed 60 months. Source selection procedures will be used to evaluate and select the proposal that is most advantageous to the Government. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this procurement is 562111 and the annual size standard is $47,000,000.00. The proposed contract listed here is being considered for a set-aside. Interested small business concerns should indicate interest by providing evidence to demonstrate the capability to perform the requirements and a positive statement of eligibility as a small business concern. If adequate interest is not received from small business concerns, the solicitation will be issued as unrestricted without further notice. The capabilities package shall not exceed 10 pages and, at a minimum, address the following: (1) Examples of projects worked within the last five years of similar size/value, scope, and complexity as the work indicated; include a brief description of how the referenced contract work relates to the work described. Indicate whether your firm worked as a prime or subcontractor. Size: A maintenance service contract with a yearly value of at least $2M or greater per year for recurring services. Indefinite Quantity / Indefinite Delivery values for infrequent work will not be considered similar in size. Scope: Demonstrate the ability to provide maintenance and repair services to a wide variety of systems and equipment, including but not limited to those listed in the General Work Requirements. Complexity: Demonstrate the ability to respond simultaneously to service call and maintenance requirements for various types of equipment, and systems at various locations and buildings throughout the installation and supporting annexes. Demonstrate the ability to manage competing priority to support customer demands. (2) Company profile, to include number of offices and number of employees per office, annual receipts, office location(s), DUNS number, and CAGE Code. (3) Type of Business: Identify whether your firm is an 8(a) Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses, Women Owned Small Businesses, Economically Disadvantaged Women Owned Small Businesses, or other Small Business concern. If you are proposing as an 8(a) mentor Prot�g�, please provide a copy of the SBA approval of the Mentor Prot�g� agreement. For more information on the definitions or requirements for these small business programs, refer to https://www.sba.gov. The capabilities package for this Sources Sought Notice is not expected to be a proposal, but rather a short statement regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate existing or developed expertise and experience in relation to this contract. Any commercial brochures or currently existing marketing material may also be submitted with the capabilities package. Submission of a capabilities package is not a pre-requisite to any potential future offerings. RESPONSES ARE DUE ON 11 SEPTEMBER 2026 BY 3:00 P.M. Eastern Time. Submissions shall ONLY be submitted electronically to Michelle Cuellar via email at michelle.l.cuellar2.civ@us.navy.mil. Submissions MUST be limited to 10Mb attachment. Responses received after the deadline or without required information will not be considered. Telephone calls will NOT be accepted. Offerors/Bidders can view and/or download the solicitation, and any attachments, at https://www.sam.gov when it becomes available.

title: OFFICE RENOVATION AT THE OFFICE LOCATED IN BELO HORIZONTE, MINAS GERAIS
description: Contractor to supply engineering services, materials, labor, tools, and equipment necessary for the successful renovation of the USG office located at Av. do Contorno, 4520, 2nd floor, Belo Horizonte, MG, Brazil, CEP 30110-028. This renovation will consist of: i) emptying the workspace, including disassembly, removal, and temporary storage of workstations and equipment; ii) demolition of existing partitions per the attached design; iii) adequation of existing electrical, IT, telephony, and TV infrastructure; iv) construction of new partitions (glass, per two design options); v) alterations and revisions to the existing Dutotec structured raceway system; vi) supply and execution of complementary electrical, IT, and telephony installations; vii) review and replacement of existing outlets, switches, and finish plates; viii) installation of new air-conditioning units and review of existing units; ix) installation of new light fixtures and drywall ceiling repair; x) general painting; xi) supply and installation of new carpet; xii) review and repair of existing blinds; xiii) reassembly of furniture and equipment; and xiv) supply of new furniture items.

title: FY 26 Roush Lake Diesel Fill Tube Replacement
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) - Chicago District is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) under solicitation number W912P626QA030. This acquisition is being conducted using Simplified Acquisition Procedures in accordance with RFO Part 13.*****This project is a Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS code 237120 (Oil and Gas Pipeline and Related Structures Construction), which carries a small business size standard of $45,000,000.00. *****The Contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, supplies, tools, and equipment necessary to complete the construction project located at J. Edward Roush Lake Dam in Huntington, Indiana (Zip Code: 46750). The required work is structured under two primary Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract Line Items (CLINs): *****CLIN 0001 (Base) - Replace Diesel Tank Fill Tube: Safe removal of the existing ~20-foot-long fuel fill tube located on a sloped embankment. Installation of a new, sealed connection from the interior 2,000-gallon tank to the road deck fill point, terminating in a lockable filler neck and cap assembly. The new fill tube must be constructed of ASTM A106, Grade B, Schedule 40 seamless carbon steel pipe. Surface preparation and application of a vinyl paint system conforming to USACE Formula V-766e in strict accordance with UFGS Section 09 97 02 (Painting: Hydraulic Structures) is required. *****CLIN 0002 (Base) - Install Emergency Vent on Diesel Tank: Correct calculation of the required venting capacity and installation of an appropriately sized, brand-approved emergency pressure relief vent on the existing 2,000-gallon diesel fuel tank located on the 3rd floor of the tower structure, in strict accordance with National Fire Protection Agency (NFPA) 30, Section 22.7. *****Warranty Requirements: In accordance with SOW Section 4.E and RFO 52.246-21 (Warranty of Construction), the Contractor shall provide a standard 1-year warranty on materials and a general 1-year warranty for installation, running from the date of final Government acceptance. *****STATUTORY SMALL BUSINESS DISCLOSURE: DEFINITIZATION OF EQUITABLE ADJUSTMENTS (RFO 36.101-4 and DFARS CD 2026-O0019)As required by 15 U.S.C. 644(w), when the Contracting Officer anticipates the award of a construction contract to a small business concern, the solicitation notice must include information regarding the agency s definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders: *****USACE Policies and Procedures: Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to USACE Partnering Details (https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/) then scrolling down on the right-hand side of the page and clicking on View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here. *****No data is available regarding the timely definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts. *****SUBMISSION MODULE and PORTAL REGISTRATION (MANDATORY)To submit a quote, your firm must be registered in the System for Award Management at SAM.gov and within the DoD Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module at PIEE Portal. *****Submission Method: Quotes must be submitted electronically via the PIEE Solicitation Module. NO OTHER TRANSMISSION METHODS (EMAIL, FACSIMILE, REGULAR MAIL, HAND CARRIED, ETC.) WILL BE ACCEPTED. Any questions regarding the PIEE portal should be directed to the PIEE Helpdesk at the portal link above. *****Site Visit Coordination: A site visit is highly recommended. To coordinate access to the J. Edward Roush Lake Dam, contact Lake Manager Wesley Millar via email at Wesley.s.millar@usace.army.mil or phone at 260-356-8648. *****Inquiries/Questions Due Date: All technical and administrative questions must be submitted via email to James Parizek at James.P.Parizek@usace.army.mil no later than September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Central Time. Please include the solicitation number in the subject line.*****Responsibility Statement: All responsible sources may submit a quotation which, if received in a timely manner, shall be considered by the agency.

title: Dismantle of Monarch Milling Machine
description: Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PHNSY & IMF) is a US Navy regional industrial center that maintains, overhauls and repairs various vessels of the US Navy. Its industrial operations provide the US naval forces with a wide range of services and resources located on the island of Oahu, Hawaii, with direct and indirect support to submarines, surface vessels and shore based activities in the Pacific. PHNSY & IMF requires a contractor to remove and dismantle one (1) Monarch Milling Machine located in an industrial shop facility. The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, tools, design, transportation and machinery to remove, dismantle and palletize one (1) Monarch Milling Machine. The contractor shall provide one individual as a Project Manager who is responsible for the planning, scheduling and managing the execution of all aspects of the work required. Additional details and specifications can be found in the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). The tentative period of performance for this service is 9/28/2026 �5/27/2027. description: Sources Sought Notice for USACE National Enterprise Dredging Center Small Business Dredging Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) This is a Sources Sought/Request for Information only. This is NOT a Solicitation Announcement, nor is it a Request for Proposal. This request does not obligate the Government in any contract award. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Enterprise Dredging Center plans to award a multiple task order contract (MATOC) for maintenance dredging within the Boundaries of the United States. This contract will be established primarily to serve the boundaries of the United States area of responsibility. The maximum number of contract awards will be dependent upon the number of offerors whose proposals the Source Selection Authority determines meets the requirements of acceptability as set forth in the solicitation. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) executes construction contracts for regular, reoccurring, and emergency National Enterprise Dredging requirements at various coastal harbors, inland rivers, canals, and connecting channels throughout the United States. Individual projects are typically annual requirements and may utilize mechanical, hydraulic, or a combination of dredging equipment and techniques with activities to include but not limited to maintenance and new work dredging, dredged material placement, and other activities such as Confined Disposal Facility (CDF), Dredged Material Disposal Facility (DMDF), or upland containment facility maintenance, groundskeeping, other earthwork at placement sites, surveying, or other work connected with dredging and placement requirements. Task orders issued under this MATOC will require the contractor to mobilize dredge plant and support vessels to the project location, perform dredging as shown on the respective plan(s), place dredged material�which may include beach nourishment, open-water placement, CDFs, DMDFs, beneficial use, or alternative placement strategies as indicated in individual task orders�and demobilize once complete. The solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be posted on the Sam.gov website at https://sam.gov/. In order to receive notification of any amendments to this solicitation, interested vendors must REGISTER AS AN INTERESTED VENDOR on the Sam.gov website at https://sam.gov/. If you are not registered, the Government is not responsible with providing you with notification of any amendments to this solicitation. You must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) in order to be eligible to receive an award from this solicitation. For additional information, please call 866-606-8220 or visit the SAM website at https://www.sam.gov/. NAICS Code 237990 Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities, size standard $37 million. NOTE: TO BE CONSIDERED A SMALL BUSINESS, A FIRM MUST PERFORM AT LEAST 40 PERCENT OF THE VOLUME DREDGED WITH ITS OWN EQUIPMENT OR EQUIPMENT OWNED BY ANOTHER SMALL BUSINESS (13 CFR 121). The maximum ordering capacity for the 5-year ordering period of the MATOC and maximum task order amounts are TBD. description: The Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) is responsible for countering international crime, illegal drugs, and instability abroad to make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous, while securing our borders and strengthening international partners for the US Department of State (DOS). In this Statement of Work, INL - El Salvador is supporting the National Academy of Public Security (ANSP) in its efforts to modernize classrooms and offices used for videoconferences at the San Luis Talpa campus. The acquisition of monitors, cameras, large-format displays, scanning equipment, laptop computers, audio systems, wireless microphones, software, and related accessories addresses a capability gap in digital training and institutional coordination infrastructure. This project enhances virtual learning environments, improves operational readiness for remote and hybrid training activities, and builds sustainable capacity for more effective academy instruction.

description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE Cyber Maintenance Hangar Modernization � Mansfield, OH Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market research and informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million 1. PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District plans to issue a solicitation for either the new construction of an ICD-705 compliant endo-skeleton structure within an existing hangar OR new ICD-705 compliant prefabricated panelized facility to house Cyber Warfare Operations within an existing hangar. The project will provide cyber operations space within the existing bay. The awardee will construct all spaces to the appropriate security levels, install communications room to accommodate servers and equipment, provide all supporting electrical, mechanical, security, life safety, fire alarm and sprinkler systems, and communications supporting infrastructure, and provide emergency power systems and standby generator connection. High-Security Spaces (ICD 705): Renovation and construction of Special Access Program (SAP) spaces and Secure Compartmentalized Information Facilities (SCIFs) built to stringent ICD 705 standards along with potential deconstruction of existing Hangar Door to achieve and maintain ICD-705 compliant perimeter. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $50,000,000 (Phase 2) Funding Source: Operations & Maintenance (O&M) 2. PLANNED ACQUISITION STRATEGY The Government is considering utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement for a prototype project under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies or delivery methodologies to achieve benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. The baseline delivery method under consideration is Progressive Design-Build (PDB). Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): The Government and the OT Awardee will work collaboratively to advance the design, perform constructability reviews, conduct open-book cost estimating, and mitigate project risks. Phase 2 (Construction): Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design (e.g., 60% to 90%), the Awardee will propose a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). If accepted, the Government will exercise Phase 2 for construction execution. If a GMP cannot be agreed upon, the Government retains an "off-ramp" to complete the design and construct the facility via alternative methods. Alternative Under Consideration: The Government is also evaluating a Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) delivery method under the OTA framework, particularly in scenarios where the Government-appointed Architect-Engineer (A-E) / Designer of Record (DOR) is pre-selected and dictated to the constructor. 3. INFORMATION REQUESTED Section 1: Company Profile Firm Name, Address, and Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email). Unique Entity ID (UEI). Socioeconomic Status (Other than Small, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone, etc.). Section 2: Other Transaction Authority (OTA) & Statutory Compliance Innovative Technologies & Practices: 10 U.S.C. � 2808a focuses on prototyping with emergent construction technologies or innovative processes. Describe any innovative materials, sustainable building technologies, or modern construction processes (e.g., prefabrication, modular MEP systems, etc.) your firm could utilize to accelerate the schedule, reduce costs, and increase the building's life expectancy. Please provide a brief (no more than 1 page) description of your general approach to and the cost/pricing implications of the following: 1) new construction of an endo skeleton structure within an existing hangar to house Cyber Warfare Operations; and 2) providing new ICD-705 compliant �prefabricated trailers� to house Cyber Warfare Operations within an existing hangar. The information you provide regarding these various approaches will help the Government determine an appropriate path forward to successful execution of the project within funding limitations. OTA Experience: Describe your firm�s experience (if any) executing projects under an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). Overcoming Traditional Barriers: What commercial or Government-imposed barriers (e.g., traditional FAR-based procurement limitations) make it difficult to implement innovative methods on complex military renovations? How can the flexibility of an OTA help overcome these barriers? Section 3: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) / Early Contractor Involvement Information Baseline: What minimum level of detail (e.g., DD Form 1391, conceptual design, spatial programming documents) does your firm require prior to entering Phase 1 (Design & Pre-construction) to feel confident in the project's baseline viability and target budget? Collaborative Framework: What collaborative mechanisms (such as joint design charrettes, target-value design workshops, or phased scoping approvals) do you recommend the Government implement in the first 30-90 days of Phase 1 to rapidly transition from a planning document to an agreed-upon technical baseline? Open-Book Pricing: Describe your experience with and internal processes involved in "open-book" pricing and transparency during pre-construction. How will you assure the Government that subcontractor and material pricing represent fair market value? Section 4: DESIGN PARTNER (A-E/DOR) TEAMING & DELIVERY METHOD ALTERNATIVES The Government is seeking targeted feedback on the structuring of design teams and alternative delivery methods (PDB vs. CMAR) for this complex headquarters renovation. Dictated A-E / Designer of Record (DOR): If the Government dictates the A-E firm / DOR for this project (e.g., a pre-selected firm already familiar with the facility's design/planning documents), rather than allowing your firm to team with an A-E of your own choosing, would your firm still be interested in bidding as the Prime Contractor? Please explain your reasoning. What major risks, operational friction, or coordination challenges do you foresee with a government-dictated A-E model? How would your firm mitigate those risks? PDB vs. CMAR Strategy: If the A-E/DOR is dictated by the Government, does this change your perspective on the viability of the Progressive Design-Build (PDB) w/ OTA strategy? Would a Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) w/ OTA strategy be a better, more appropriate fit for this project if the designer is pre-selected? Please contrast the advantages and disadvantages of PDB vs. CMAR under a government-dictated design team structure. Section 5: Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP), Risk Allocation & Compensation Off-Ramp Risk & Design Rights: If the Government and the contractor cannot reach an agreement on the Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP), and the decision is made to �off ramp�, what specific compensation structures (e.g., design fees, stipends, time-and-materials) would adequately compensate your firm for Phase 1 efforts? title: Perforated Window Film
description: This contract is in support of the United States Marine Corps Recruiting Command (MCRC) Branding Program for each of the six (6) Marine Corps Districts (MCD), which are located throughout the United States, overseas and its territories. The use of branded locations, emphasizing the approved Marine Corps colors, symbols, themes, furnishings, and lighting effects will help distinguish Marine Corps recruiting offices from recruiting offices of other Armed Services, providing a distinct recruiting advantage vis-a-vis other Services. The appearance of the branded offices leaves a positive impression not just with prospects, but their parents and other influencers as well. MCRC is taking steps to improve physical security of recruiting facilities. MCRC intends to utilize perforated window film on the glass surfaces of storefront recruiting facilities in order to provide concealment, more specifically, protection from observation. It is necessary to have a means of obscuring the view of Marine recruiting station from the outside as a force protection measure. It is also necessary that, where practical, the Marines maintain visibility of the area outside of their office in order to maintain their situational awareness. This will provide them with the possibility of early warning, if a potential aggressor is approaching the office or preparing to commit some type of hostile or unlawful act, outside the office. Perforated window film will allow for MCRC Branding Program success, while providing increased security for recruiting personnel and individuals visiting recruiting offices. As a part of this requirement, the current storefront glass graphics will be removed, and new perforated window film will be installed to span the entire glass window/door surface. Perforated window film will be installed on existing facilities that have no storefront graphics. Additionally, perforated film will be replaced on existing facilities as required.

title: UPGRADE ENTRANCE PORTAL AT BROOHAVEN NATIONAL LABORATORY
description: Amendment No. 3 (dated 8/26/26) provides responses to vendor questions. Use the shared link provided in this notice to access the contract documents, including all amendments. Amendment No. 2 (dated 8/25/26) provides responses to vendor questions and extends the Offer Due Date from 9/8/26 to 9/11/26. Use the shared link provided in this notice to access the contract documents, including all amendments. Amendment No. 1 (dated 8/17/26) provides responses to vendor questions. Use the shared link provided in this notice to access the contract documents, including all amendments. Brookhaven Science Associates, LLC (BSA), the Management and Operating (M&O) contractor for Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL), intends to construct a new entrance portal at the Laboratory's primary entrance. The existing Main Gate security access point (Building 680), constructed in 1960, has exceeded its useful service life and requires replacement. The project will replace the existing entrance and provide a modernized entrance portal featuring fully integrated security booths to monitor, screen, and process personnel and vehicular traffic entering the Laboratory. The new portal will provide weather protection for security personnel, enhanced site lighting, and a modern traffic control system designed to improve safety, efficiency, and operational reliability. The upgraded entrance will also complement the adjacent, publicly accessible Science and User Support Center (SUSC) by providing a secure, efficient, and welcoming point of entry to the Laboratory. The scope of work for the contract includes the demolition and removal of the existing security booths and associated infrastructure, and the construction of a new entrance portal facility, including structural systems, utilities, security systems, site improvements, and all supporting infrastructure required for full operational capability. BSA will furnish two (2) prefabricated security booths as Government-Furnished Property (GFP). Solicitation documents are available at the link provided in this notice. title: W023-- Northwoods National Cemetery Office Trailer Lease
description: NORTHWOODS NATIONAL CEMETERY Office Trailer Lease Performance of Work Statement General Scope Northwoods National Cemetery has a requirement for a temporary office trailer for a period of twelve months to be provided in accordance with the terms and conditions outlined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS). Goal The primary objective of this contract is to provide temporary office space for one employee at Northwoods National Cemetery, located at 4520 Lakewood Rd, Harshaw, WI 54529. The contractor will be responsible for providing all required aspects of a 12 month trailer lease, including delivery, setup, and removal. General Requirements The Contractor shall provide a temporary office trailer for a period of 12 months as well as all transportation, labor, parts, and materials to deliver, setup, secure, dismantle and remove at the end of the lease. SPECIFICATIONS The following list, with subsequent corresponding descriptions of services, covers the types and delivery frequencies of services that will be required for fulfillment of this contract. The Contractor shall coordinate with the CO or COR as appropriate to determine delivery schedules, and the trailer placement location. Line-Item Number Section Description 0001 A.1.1 Delivery and setup of office trailer, skirting and steps 0002 A.1.2 Monthly fee for lease 0003 A.1.3 Dismantling, removal and return A.1.1 Delivery and setup of office trailer, skirting and steps: Prior to shipping, the contractor will notify the COR/CO and provide the government with the opportunity to verify the trailer meets the requirements. This inspection can take place either remotely or in-person. The trailer must not be shipped prior to this verification by the government. If the government finds the trailer does not meet the requirements the contractor shall provide an alternative trailer for inspection within 2 weeks (10 business days). The contractor shall provide all resources required to deliver, set up, and properly secure the trailer, skirting and steps. Final inspection and acceptance by the COR/CO will take place when the trailer is ready for occupancy. A.1.2 Monthly fee for lease: The monthly lease fee must include all reoccurring charges associated with the lease of the trailer including stairs, skirting, and all materials or equipment provided. A.1.3 Dismantling, removal and return: The contractor shall provide all resources required to dismantle and remove the trailer and all associated materials and equipment provided by the contractor. Office Trailer requirements: The contractor shall provide an office trailer of not less than 160 gross square feet that is designed and built for. The trailer must be in new or in as new condition but in no cases more than 3 years old. Trailers that are dirty, stained, discolored, have visible prior damage, or in disrepair will not be accepted. Installation of the office must meet all local and state codes for the town of Harshaw, Oneida County, Wisconsin. The minimum requirements are: 160 gross square feet Three-foot wide exterior door, including hardware. ADA ramp meeting all local, state and Federal ADA regulations for the town of Harshaw, Oneida County, Wisconsin. 2 operable windows that can be opened for ventilation. OSHA approved platform and stairs leading to grade. Skirting the entire perimeter of the office from the floor to the ground that matches the color and material of the exterior of the trailer Exterior finishes shall be visually pleasing to the eye and not detract from the solemnity and decorum of a national cemetery (i.e. Bright colors and large or attention-grabbing designs should be avoided) Provide floor, wall, and roof with insulation as follows: R-19 within the floor, R-13 within exterior walls, R-38 within the roof Interior finishes shall consist of resilient flooring, plywood paneling or painted wallboard on walls, and acoustical tile ceilings. Provide sufficient fluorescent lighting to deliver 70 foot-candles of light at desktop height without the aid of daylight. Provide one light switch Provide one duplex receptacle on each wall. If a wall is 10 feet long or more, provide two receptacles for each 10 feet, or portion thereof, of wall Thermostatically controlled, centralized heating and air conditioning system designed to maintain the temperature between 70- and 80-degrees F with 50 percent relative humidity maintained during the air conditioning season. Provide maintenance or repair services within 72 hours of notification. Contractor s Representative: Upon contract award, the Contractor shall promptly provide the Contracting Officer (CO) with the name and contact information of the individual designated as the Contractor s Representative for this contract. The Contractor s Representative shall have overall management responsibility for the execution of all contract requirements and shall serve as the primary point of contact for day-to-day operations, receiving technical direction, and addressing issues that arise under the contract. This individual shall also be responsible for coordinating and communicating matters of mutual concern with Government representatives. The Contractor s Representative may appoint a designated inspector or liaison to work directly with the Government on operational matters subject to the approval of the CO. Regulatory Compliance, Permits, Licenses: The Contractor shall obtain and maintain all applicable licenses, permits, and certifications necessary to perform the work required under this contract prior to the commencement of performance. All such licenses and permits shall be current and valid throughout the contract term. Upon request, the Contractor shall provide the Contracting Officer with copies of all licenses and permits. The Contractor shall, at no expense to the Government, be responsible for obtaining and maintaining all necessary licenses and permits and for complying with all applicable Federal, State, and municipal laws, codes, and regulations governing the performance of the contract. Verification of Service: The Contractor shall submit all monthly invoices via the Tungsten e-Invoice Network. Copies of each invoice shall be forwarded to the Contracting Officer s Representative (COR) for verification. The COR shall review each invoice to verify that services invoiced conform to contract requirements. In the event services were not delivered or invoiced incorrectly, the COR will document the discrepancies in writing and forward such documentation to the Contracting Officer (CO). The Cemetery certifying official will then contact the Contractor to resolve the issue and/or return the invoice for correction. If the COR does not contact the Contractor regarding any discrepancies within a reasonable timeframe, it shall be assumed the invoice is accurate and approved for payment. The Cemetery will retain copies of all approved invoices for their records and for future reference. Payments shall be made via electronic funds transfer (EFT) through the Tungsten e-Invoice Network following invoice approval. Inspection of Services: Definitions: For purposes of this clause, Services includes all services performed, workmanship, and materials furnished or utilized in the performance of the contract. The Contractor shall establish and maintain an inspection system acceptable to the Government covering all services performed under this contract. The Contractor shall maintain complete records of all inspection activities and shall make these records available to the Government during contract performance and for such period thereafter as may be required. The Government reserves the right to inspect and test all services called for by the contract at all reasonable times and locations during the contract term. Such inspections and tests shall be conducted in a manner that does not unreasonably delay the Contractor s performance. End of Scope

This effort requires the Contractor to furnish qualified subject matter experts to assist the Government and its partners with integration, testing, diagnostics, and troubleshooting of the Improved Bradley Acquisition Subsystem (IBAS) and the TOW 2 Subsystem (T2SS) at the Cherokee Nations facility in Huntsville, AL. This requirement supports the Bradley Fighting Vehicle by sustaining the Bradley Fire Control Subsystems, including the Improved Bradley Acquisition Subsystem (IBAS) and the TOW 2 Subsystem (T2SS). Required support includes system integration and checkout, fault isolation and diagnostics, test and validation assistance, and real-time technical guidance to Government and Cherokee Nations personnel. Deliverables consist of weekly status reports documenting progress and a final technical summary report outlining subsystem status, resolved and unresolved issues, and recommendations for continued sustainment. title: Market Survey - Controller Training Solutions (CTS) II
description: This Request for Information (RFI) for Air Traffic Controller (ATC) training is being issued in accordance with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Acquisition Management System (AMS) Policy 3.2.1.2.1. Responses to this RFI will be used for informational purposes only to support the development of a contracting strategy for ATC training. The information will not be released except as required under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). Proprietary information will be protected if appropriately marked. This is not a Screening Information Request or Request for Proposal. The purpose of this announcement is to obtain industry feedback on an updated acquisition strategy as well as the application of innovative training technologies and models for the next generation of ATC Training Support Services program. Historically, these complex training services�encompassing institutional classroom instruction, simulation laboratory support, and curriculum maintenance and development at the FAA Academy and field facilities�have been procured using a Time & Materials (T&M) contract structure for everything other than Program Management activities. Currently, the contract supports two primary locations for instruction: FAA Academy (~40% of value under T&M): Centralized foundational training and workforce development. Field Facilities (~60% of value under T&M): Localized delivery across 300+ nationwide sites (EnRoute centers, TRACONs, and airport control towers). Executive Order 14402 �Promoting Efficiency, Accountability, and Performance in Federal Contracting,� directs Federal agencies to prioritize fixed-price (FP) contracts with performance-based considerations to improve efficiency, accountability, and cost control in government procurement. In alignment with this policy, the FAA intends to transition to a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract structure for its ATC training support requirements. The FAA seeks specific industry feedback on how to best structure a future ATC training contract as a FFP vehicle to ensure the continued delivery of world-class training while mitigating cost overruns and performance risks. Additionally, the FAA requests industry feedback on designing a FFP structure that incentivizes contractors throughout the period of performance to continuously identify, evaluate, and integrate innovative methods, technologies, tools, and curricula (such as but not limited to advanced simulation, AI-driven adaptive learning, or updated instruction techniques) without requiring costly or complex contract modifications. Related announcements include: CTS-II-MarketSurvey-001 and 693KA8-25-R-00013

title: W50SLF26QA014 - Optimizing the Human Weapon System
description: The Hawaii Air National Guard is requesting for quotations for their OHWS requirement. Quotations are due via email to Emma Newbegin, emma.a.newbegin.civ@army.mil, no later than 1000AM HST, 11 September 2026. Questions regarding the solicitation are due by 12:00 PM Hawaii Standard Time on Tuesday, 18 August, 2026. Electronic quotations must be submitted via e-mail to Emma Newbegin at emma.a.newbegin.civ@army.mil. Information provided from answers to questions shall not change/qualify the terms and conditions of the solicitation and specifications. Terms remain unchanged unless the solicitation is amended in writing. if an amendment is issued, normal procedure relating to the acknowledgment and receipt of solcitation amendments shall apply. REQUIREMENT SCOPE (see attached PWS for full details): The purpose of the OHWS program is to reduce the frequency and severity of neck and back pain injuries, reduce duty time lost, improve quality of life, enhance readiness, and support fighter aircrew retention. The Contractor goal is to reduce injury rates and to increase the rate of fighter aircrew fully mission capable status. This OHWS program is intended to produce retention on a system-wide basis and is described as prehabilitation. Prehabilitation involves prevention of disability and pain experienced as a result of fighter operations through a program specifically designed to train and otherwise prepare aircrew for the rigorous demands of fighters. This program will target specific neck and back strength and conditioning training which will best prepare the aircrew. In addition, overall conditioning and health education, designed to bring aircrew to the peak of fitness, will further decrease the incidence and severity of neck and back problems. Further, through a program of data collection, to include objective and subjective information, the program will evolve as needed to ensure all efforts for improving the quality of life for aircrew are flexible and continue to be optimized. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the solicitation is 541990 � All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services Contractors with a small business size standard of $19,500,000. Place of Performance: The work will be performed at the Hawaii Air National Guard Campus, Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH), HI 96853. Period of Performance: The estimated period of performance base year plus four option years, tentatively scheduled to start from September 30, 2026, to September 29, 2031. Solicitations shall not exceed 5 pages, and provide the following: One (1) signed copy of the Solicitation (SF1449) Vendor Name, Vendor POC, Vendor CAGE, Vendor UEI, Contact Ph#, E-mail, Discount terms (if applicable); Socio-Economic status; and completed Work Experience Form (attached) Additionally, in order to be eligible for award, all respondents shall complete all Representations and Certifications found within their profile in the System of Award Management (SAM) at https://www.sam.gov. The Government intends to evaluate offers and award a contract WITHOUT discussions with offerors. Therefore, the offeror's inital offer should contain the offeror's best terms. [RFO FAR 52.212-1(d)]. A quoter which requires the Government to execute a separate agreement with a third party shall be deemed technically unacceptable. Facsimile quotations will not be accepted.

PLEASE NOTE - IF YOU HAVE NOT YET SUBMITTED A REQUEST FOR ACCESS TO THE ATTACHMENTS, PLEASE READ THE FOLLOWING: When you submit your request for access to the attachments, please make sure you provide the CMMC UID for each contractor information system that will store the attachments of this RFI. Purpose: The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gauge industry interest and capability in performing portions of the Performance Work Statement (PWS) on a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) basis to support the Atlantic Undersea Test and Evaluation Center (AUTEC) contract. The PWS is grouped by three separate operation groups: Base Operations, Enterprise Operations, and Test Operations. The current contract number is N6660422C0102, and the prime contractor is Amentum Services Inc. AUTEC is the U.S. Navy�s Large-Area, Deep-Water, Undersea T&E Range within DoD�s Major Range and Test Facility Base (MRTFB). The range is located at Andros Island, Commonwealth of the Bahamas (AUTEC/Andros). The contract requires the contractor to supply a highly capable technical workforce who will operate and maintain unique tracking and instrumentation systems to support Navy Developmental and Fleet Training and Readiness Missions. Additionally, the contract establishes the contractor responsible for operation of a self-sufficient one square mile Navy outpost. The tasking is summarized at a high-level as follows: Base Operations on the AUTEC contract includes public works, logistic support, the maintenance/repair/construction of real property and grounds for AUTEC/Andros sites, Permanent-Party Housing, food services, emergency and firefighting services, and solid waste and recycling, in addition to other operation services (please review the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS) for further details). Enterprise Operations encompasses all functions related to General Information Management and Services sustaining AUTEC in the performance of its mission. title: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) Survey for the Construction of an Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) and Vehicle Maintenance Shop (VMS) on Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska
description: THIS IS A PROJECT LABOR AGREEMENT (PLA) SURVEY ONLY. *****No proposals are being requested or accepted with this PLA notice.***** This is a SPECIAL NOTICE. The Corps of Engineers Louisville District is soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLAs) for a large-scale construction project ($35 million or more) for the following: Project scope: This project is a Design-Bid-Build and will construct a collocated Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) and Vehicle Maintenance Shop (VMS) on Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska. Building design(s) will comply with Unified Facilities Criteria, UFC 4-171-05, Army Reserve Facilities. Supporting facilities include land clearing, paving, concrete aprons, vehicle wash rack/platform, bi-level equipment loading ramp, fencing, general site improvements and utility connections. Accessibility for the disabled will be provided. Antiterrorism/Force Protection (AT/FP) and physical security measures will be incorporated into the design including maximum standoff distances from roads, parking areas and vehicle unloading areas. Contract duration is estimated at 1,095 calendar days. The estimated cost range is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. NAICS code is 236220. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C. 158(f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Policy: 1. FAR 22.502 requires agencies to use Project Labor Agreement (PLA) in large-scale construction projects to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. 2. An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will: 1) Advance the Federal Governments interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and 2) Be consistent with law. References: Provision: 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement Clause: 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. 3. In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the construction community is invited to comment on the use of PLAs. Of particular interest to the Government are responses to the following questions: Do you have knowledge that a PLA has been used in the local area on projects of this kind? If so, please provide supporting documentation. Are you aware of skilled labor shortages in the area for those crafts that will be needed to complete the referenced project? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. Are you aware of time sensitive issues/scheduling requirements that would affect the rate at which the referenced project should be completed? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. Identify specific reasons why or how you believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. Identify specific reasons why you do not believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. Identify any additional information you believe should be considered on the use of a PLA on the referenced project. Identify any additional information you believe should be considered on the non-use of a PLA on the referenced project. The information gathered in this exercise should include the following information on projects completed in the last 2-5 years (or other timeframe, as appropriate): Project Name and Location Detailed Project Description Initial Cost Estimate vs. Actual Final Cost Was the project completed on time? Number of craft trades present on the project Was a PLA used? Were there any challenges experienced during the project? Please select one of the following: My company will not submit a proposal if PLA is required. My company plans to submit a proposal whether PLA is required or not. My company only plans to submit a proposal if PLA is required. 4. In addition to affirmative responses, we are seeking negative responses to identify any potential actions we may take to improve the competitive environment. Please provide a response with feedback including rationale for not wanting to submit a proposal and any recommendations that could promote interest. Please provide your comments via e-mail to Ethan.S.Phillips@usace.army.mil no later than 4:00 PM Eastern Time on 11 September 2026.

Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. title: Blast Overpressure Sensor System (BOSS)
description: 1. Background: Through three National Defense Authorization Acts (NDAA), Section 734 of the 2018 NDAA, Section 253 of the 2019 NDAA, and Sections 717 and 742 of the 2020 NDAA, Congress mandated longitudinal medical studies on Blast Overpressure (BOP) exposure. These studies aim to improve the DoD�s understanding of how blast exposure affects Service Members� brain health and to better inform policies on risk mitigation, unit readiness, and health care decisions. The BOSS will be a Soldier-worn device designed to track, store, and transmit blast overpressure events caused by shock waves above normal atmospheric pressure, whether from tier-one weapons or explosions during training and combat. By proactively monitoring blast exposure, BOSS may help reduce injury severity. It will provide real-time data to inform medical decisions and maintain exposure history for long-term health monitoring within the PEO Soldier Data Eco-System. 2. Objective and Purpose/Scope: The Government intends to conduct a Sources Sought to identify qualified sources capable of meeting the required Key Performance Parameters (KPPs), as well as to gain an understanding of how potential vendors may be able to meet these requirements in the future. Through this market research effort, the Government seeks to assess current industry capability, evaluate associated risks, and determine the feasibility and maturity of potential paths toward full KPP compliance. The information received will help the Government shape acquisition planning, refine requirements, and better understand the solutions available or emerging within industry. 3. Submission Instructions: Response Due Date: Interested parties shall submit the RFI response electronically by 1600 Eastern on 11 September 2026 via e-mail to: roxanne.a.dalrymple.civ@army.mil; timothy.j.compton7.civ@army.mil Email Subject/Title: "RFI response for W91CRB-26-RFI-BOSS" Format: Microsoft Word or searchable Adobe PDF. Arial 12-point font, single spaced, single sided, 8.5 by 11-inch paper with 1-inch margins. Required Contents: Cover Page (1-page limit) including Title, Organization, Technical and administrative points of contact (names, addresses, phone, fax number and email addresses), and Topic area: "TITLE". Completed Attachment 1 (BOSS Requirement Document) and Attachment 2 (BOSS Remarks). The response shall provide sufficient technical data to determine how you fully meet the requirements. 4. Disclaimer: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS (RFQ); IT IS STRICTLY A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI). This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and is neither to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. NO PHONE CALLS WILL BE ACCEPTED OR RETURNED. All 'Proprietary', 'Classified', 'Confidential', or 'Sensitive' information shall be marked as such and will be treated accordingly. 5.
