title: ATC Turf Field Maintenance
description: The objective of this contract is to provide comprehensive maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson. The Contractor shall furnish all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to perform turf field grooming, preventive maintenance, minor repair services, and unscheduled/emergency maintenance. Scheduled maintenance shall be performed bi-annually to ensure proper turf condition, safety, and performance. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Fort Jackson, South Carolina 29207 BASIS FOR AWARD: The Government will utilize a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation method for this requirement. The Government will award one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) C-Type contract to the offeror whose proposal is technically acceptable, has the lowest evaluated price, and is deemed responsible. The Government will evaluate the contractor's Technical Approach, Past Performance, and Price Proposal to ensure that it reflects a sound understanding of this requirement and complies with the requirements in the solicitation. A determination of a fair and reasonable price will be conducted. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Offerors shall submit a signed and dated proposal electronically in accordance with the attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-1 Instructions. Failure to provide all required documents or information may exclude the offeror from further consideration. Proposal Preparation Instructions. The solicitation instructions identify the following proposal volumes: a. Volume 1 � General b. Volume 2 � Technical Approach (to include Capabilities Statement) c. Volume 3 � Past Performance Information d. Volume 4 � Cost/Price EVALUATION: The proposal will be evaluated under three (3) evaluation factors: Factor 1: Technical Factor 2: Past Performance Factor 3: Cost/Price The Technical factor will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. An �Unacceptable� rating in any single Technical element will result in an overall rating of �Unacceptable� for Factor 1. Past Performance will be evaluated as described below. Price will be evaluated for reasonableness. See attached ADDENDUM TO RFO FAR CLAUSE 52.212-2 Evaluations. Factor 1 � Technical: The Technical factor evaluation provides an assessment of the offeror's capability to satisfy the Government's minimum requirements. The Technical factor has three elements. The Government will evaluate the technical approach, quality controls, and key personnel qualifications related to providing preventive and unscheduled maintenance for fifteen (15) artificial turf fields located throughout Fort Jackson, SC. Element 1: Technical Approach and Understanding The proposal must demonstrate a clear understanding of and a sound approach to performing all services outlined in the PWS, including the specific basic services and tasks described in PWS Part 5. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 1. PWS Compliance: A compliant, clear operational methodology to perform multi-leveling field vacuuming, extensive fiber brush grooming, use of magnetic metal sweepers, and specialized synthetic turf cleaning/sanitization across the fifteen (15) synthetic fields. 2. Operational Responsiveness: A solid approach to executing scheduled semi-annual services and mobilizing personnel/equipment for unscheduled emergency repairs/maintenance in accordance with the response timelines set forth in the PWS. Element 2: Deliverables and Quality Control The proposal must address the deliverables listed in Technical Exhibit B and include the development of a Quality Control Plan (QCP) in accordance with PWS Paragraph 1.5.1. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must prove: 3. Reporting & Deliverables Compliance: A compliant administrative framework to compile, track, and electronically deliver all semi-annual reporting, worksheets, and documentation specified in PWS Technical Exhibit B. 4. QCP Framework: A draft Quality Control Plan (QCP) that completely addresses all requirements and criteria outlined in PWS Paragraph 1.5.1, such as lines of authority, deficiency prevention, inspection logging, key controls, and records preservation. Element 3: Key Personnel The proposal must confirm that all Key Personnel meet the minimum qualifications specified in the PWS. To be rated Acceptable, the proposal must confirm: 5. PWS Qualifications & Experience: All proposed key personnel meet the minimum standards specified in PWS Paragraph 1.10. This includes confirming that the Contract Manager/Alternate has full authority to act on daily operations, and the Quality Control Manager and Systems Administrator each possess a minimum of five (5) years of direct experience. 6. Special Qualifications: Proof that proposed staff possess and maintain active Information Assurance Technician (IAT) Level I professional certifications as required by PWS Paragraph 1.10.d. Technical Factor Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal meets the minimum requirements of the solicitation. UNACCEPTABLE � Technical Proposal does not meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. Note: An "Unacceptable" rating in any single element will result in an overall rating of "Unacceptable" for Factor 1. Factor 2 � Past Performance: The past performance evaluation will assess the offeror's probability of meeting the solicitation's requirements as indicated by that offeror's record of past performance. Past Performance is assessed at the factor level after evaluating aspects of the offeror's recent (within the last 3 years) and relevant past performance, focusing on services similar to the Turf Field Maintenance requirements. The Government will evaluate past performance based on information submitted per the solicitation instructions and other available sources. Past Performance Evaluation Ratings: ACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has a reasonable expectation that the offeror will successfully perform the required effort, or the offeror's performance record is unknown. UNACCEPTABLE � Based on the offeror's performance record, the Government has no reasonable expectation that the offeror will be able to successfully perform the required effort. NEUTRAL � In the case of an offeror without a record of relevant past performance or for whom information on past performance is not available, the offeror may not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably on past performance. In the context of acceptability/unacceptability, a "Neutral" rating shall be considered "Acceptable." Factor 3 � Cost/Price: The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total proposed price for all performance periods (Base Period plus Option Years 1 through 4). The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the base period and option period prices are significantly unbalanced. As part of price evaluation, the Government will evaluate its option to extend services under RFO FAR Clause 52.217-8 by adding one-half (1/2) of the Offeror's final option year price (Option Year 4) to the Offeror's total evaluated price. Base Period Price (CLIN 0001) Option Year 1 Price (CLIN 1001) Option Year 2 Price (CLIN 2001) Option Year 3 Price (CLIN 3001) Option Year 4 Price (CLIN 4001) Evaluation of 52.217-8 Option Price (equivalent to 1/2 of Option Year 4 price) Offerors are not required to enter a separate price for the six-month extension period. Award will be made to the responsible offeror found to be technically acceptable with the lowest total evaluated price. QUESTIONS DUE: 08SEPT2026 NLT 1200 EST. The current 52.212-1 addendum requires written questions no later than five (5) days after the solicitation announcement release date. Questions shall reference Solicitation Number W9124C26QA024, Questions and/or Comments ATC Turf Field Maintenance. PROPOSAL DUE: 11SEPT2026

title: Blast Overpressure Sensor System (BOSS)
description: Addition of Missing Attachment: "RFI Attachment 2 � Blast Overpressure Sensor System (BOSS) Remarks.xlsx" has been added to the solicitation on SAM.gov. Action Required: As stated in Section 3 (Submission Instructions), vendors must utilize and complete this Excel file as part of their response package. Clarification of Requirement Document: "RFI Attachment 1- Blast Overpressure Sensor System (BOSS) Requirement Document.docx" remains a mandatory attachment. Vendors must review this document to understand the Key Performance Parameters (KPPs) and Critical Logistic Specifications (CLS) required to formulate a complete response. 1. Background: Through three National Defense Authorization Acts (NDAA), Section 734 of the 2018 NDAA, Section 253 of the 2019 NDAA, and Sections 717 and 742 of the 2020 NDAA, Congress mandated longitudinal medical studies on Blast Overpressure (BOP) exposure. These studies aim to improve the DoD�s understanding of how blast exposure affects Service Members� brain health and to better inform policies on risk mitigation, unit readiness, and health care decisions. The BOSS will be a Soldier-worn device designed to track, store, and transmit blast overpressure events caused by shock waves above normal atmospheric pressure, whether from tier-one weapons or explosions during training and combat. By proactively monitoring blast exposure, BOSS may help reduce injury severity. It will provide real-time data to inform medical decisions and maintain exposure history for long-term health monitoring within the PEO Soldier Data Eco-System. 2. Objective and Purpose/Scope: The Government intends to conduct a Sources Sought to identify qualified sources capable of meeting the required Key Performance Parameters (KPPs), as well as to gain an understanding of how potential vendors may be able to meet these requirements in the future. Through this market research effort, the Government seeks to assess current industry capability, evaluate associated risks, and determine the feasibility and maturity of potential paths toward full KPP compliance. The information received will help the Government shape acquisition planning, refine requirements, and better understand the solutions available or emerging within industry. 3. Submission Instructions: Response Due Date: Interested parties shall submit the RFI response electronically by 1600 Eastern on 11 September 2026 via e-mail to: roxanne.a.dalrymple.civ@army.mil; timothy.j.compton7.civ@army.mil Email Subject/Title: "RFI response for W91CRB-26-RFI-BOSS" Format: Microsoft Word or searchable Adobe PDF. Arial 12-point font, single spaced, single sided, 8.5 by 11-inch paper with 1-inch margins. Required Contents: Cover Page (1-page limit) including Title, Organization, Technical and administrative points of contact (names, addresses, phone, fax number and email addresses), and Topic area: "TITLE". Completed Attachment 1 (BOSS Requirement Document) and Attachment 2 (BOSS Remarks). The response shall provide sufficient technical data to determine how you fully meet the requirements. 4. Disclaimer: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS (RFQ); IT IS STRICTLY A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI). This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and is neither to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. NO PHONE CALLS WILL BE ACCEPTED OR RETURNED. All 'Proprietary', 'Classified', 'Confidential', or 'Sensitive' information shall be marked as such and will be treated accordingly. 5. See Attachments at the bottom of this posting: Updated List of Attachments (Revision to Section 5): The complete and official list of attachments for this RFI is now updated to include the following three (3) documents: Main Solicitation Document: Boss Sources Sought.docx Attachment 1: RFI Attachment 1- Blast Overpressure Sensor System (BOSS) Requirement Document.docx Attachment 2: RFI Attachment 2 � Blast Overpressure Sensor System (BOSS) Remarks.xlsx

description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE � NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE-SOURCE Gas Analysis Services Technical Operations Need (GASTON) Notice Type: Presolicitation Notice / Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Follow-on Contract Action Code: Services - Testing Laboratories NAICS Code: 541380 (Services - Testing Laboratories) Product Service Code (PSC): H299 (Equipment and Materials Testing) Anticipated Solicitation/Contract Number: FA702226R0006 Anticipated Award Date: 15 November 2027 1. NOTICE OF INTENT The Air Force Technical Applications Center (AFTAC), Nuclear Treaty Monitoring (TT) Directorate, Patrick SFB, Florida, Contracting Office AMIC DET 2 OL/PKA intends to solicit and negotiate a sole-source, follow-on IDIQ contract with Linde Special Projects, LLC (also operating as Linde Services LLC / Linde LLC) for specialized Atmospheric Gas Analysis Services. The contract will support the Gas Analysis Services Technical Operations Need (GASTON) program. The statutory authority for this noncompetitive acquisition is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by RFO 6.302-1 (Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements). 2. TECHNICAL SUMMARY The contractor will be required to provide high-precision laboratory analytical services and research and development (R&D) support, including: Routine Sample Analysis: Gas chromatograph element assays on approximately 9,400 whole air samples annually with ?10% measurement uncertainty. Separation and Assays: High-purity separation (?99.9%) of noble gas and VOC fractions, followed by Geiger-Mueller (G-M) radiometry and Liquid-Scintillation (L-S) beta spectrometry radioassays under strict accuracy, timing, and quality-assurance controls. Engineering and GFE Maintenance: Custom software/hardware development, operations, calibration, and maintenance of specialized Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE). 3. MANDATORY CRITICAL QUALIFICATIONS Any potential source must meet the following restrictive requirements: Licensing: Possession and maintenance of an active US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) Radioactive Materials License (or agreement state license/permit) for the analytical facility. Security: Maintenance of a secure, active SECRET-rated facility cleared in accordance with DOD 5220.22-M (NISPOM), with personnel holding active final SECRET clearances eligible for access to Critical Nuclear Weapon Design Information (CNWDI) and Restricted Data (RD). 4. SUBMISSION OF CAPABILITY STATEMENTS This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation package is available. However, in accordance with the RFO Overhaul framework, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which the agency will consider. Firms that believe they can fulfill these requirements without unrecoverable duplication of cost or unacceptable national security mission delays must submit a written capability statement. Submissions must include: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, UEI, and Business Size. Direct proof of active US NRC Licensing. Verification of active cleared SECRET facility status and cleared staff (CNWDI/RD). Technical narrative demonstrating capacity to meet the GASTON performance work statement metrics. Interested parties must submit their capability packages exclusively via email to the primary contact, Contract Specialist James Fey (james.fey.1@us.af.mil), with a copy to the secondary contact, Contracting Officer Danny Austin (danny.austin.3@us.af.mil), no later than 4:00 P.M. Eastern Time (ET) on 11 September 2026. No telephone requests will be honored. SEE ATTACHMENT FOR FURTHER DETAILS For the complete list of mandatory RFO 5.101(c) data elements, detailed CLIN structures, and full technical specifications, please download and review the attached document: "Pre-Solicitation Sole Source Notice - RFO 5.101(c)".

title: Chemistry Research for the Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT)
description: The mission of National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS) is to discover how the environment affects people to promote healthier lives. The Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT) is an intramural division at NIEHS, and DTT scientists use a variety of traditional and cutting-edge approaches to better understand how factors in our environment may impact our health. One of DTT's goals is to lead the transformation of toxicology through the development and application of innovative tools and strategies. This contract will provide required chemistry research at each step of the DTT toxicological evaluation process. This acquisition is to conduct Chemistry Research for NIEHS, Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT) and National Toxicology Program (NTP). The type and extent of chemistry research support provided will be specific to DTT and NTP research needs. Program management procedures and chemistry technical activities will be provided under eight (8) Functional Areas: Logistics and Handling, Characterization, Formulation, Biosample Analysis, Special Studies, Animal Studies, Omics and In Vitro Assays. Specifications for the Conduct of Chemistry Activities for Toxicology Research Performed by the Division of Translational Toxicology at the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (DTT Chemistry Specifications): https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/data/research/chemistry/rfp

title: Chemistry Research for the Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT)
description: The mission of National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS) is to discover how the environment affects people to promote healthier lives. The Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT) is an intramural division at NIEHS, and DTT scientists use a variety of traditional and cutting-edge approaches to better understand how factors in our environment may impact our health. One of DTT's goals is to lead the transformation of toxicology through the development and application of innovative tools and strategies. This contract will provide required chemistry research at each step of the DTT toxicological evaluation process. This acquisition is to conduct Chemistry Research for NIEHS, Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT) and National Toxicology Program (NTP). The type and extent of chemistry research support provided will be specific to DTT and NTP research needs. Program management procedures and chemistry technical activities will be provided under eight (8) Functional Areas: Logistics and Handling, Characterization, Formulation, Biosample Analysis, Special Studies, Animal Studies, Omics and In Vitro Assays. Specifications for the Conduct of Chemistry Activities for Toxicology Research Performed by the Division of Translational Toxicology at the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (DTT Chemistry Specifications): https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/data/research/chemistry/rfp

title: 3D Image Reconstruction and Case Planning Services
description: The contractor shall provide 3D Image Reconstruction and Case Planning services offsite at the contractor�s facility in accordance with the specifications contained herein to eligible beneficiaries of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), North Florida/South Georgia Veterans Healthcare System, Malcom Randall VA Medical Center (hereinafter referred to as VAMC). The contractor shall perform multi?planar reformatting and 3D reconstruction of Computerized Tomography (CT) angiography studies to support case planning for vascular surgical procedures for eligible Veteran beneficiaries receiving care at the VAMC. The specific services to be performed include the acquisition, upload, and assessment of quality of digital CT Scan images and multiplanar reformatting of digital data and production of a 3D reconstruction tool for use in case planning for endovascular procedures as related to: CT Based Image Reconstruction � This includes the acquisition and assessment of digital data quality, transferring and reformatting the data to create a 3D reconstructing image suite for endovascular case planning. Provision of Secure Electronic Access � The provider shall initiate the electronic release of records to the VAMC medical records department to enable transfer of patient imaging studies using the bi?directional Medicom Imagex exchange service. The contractor shall provide secure, password?protected electronic access to the original image data, reformatted datasets, 3D reconstructed images, and associated software to support remote or urgent viewing, analysis, and case planning. Software updates and technical support � This requires regular announcement/delivery of software updates either contained within Customer Service or via online services, and the availability of technical support during regular business hours either online or via telephone. The original CT datasets for VA patients are generated on station using VA CT scanners. Data will be loaded and transmitted electronically to the Contractor for the development of the computerized interactive reconstructions in a manner consistent with VA Patient Information Security regulations. The Contractor will utilize proprietary software to transform the routine CT data into a form that allows interactive measurements and treatment device planning, ensuring the privacy, confidentiality, and security of patient data in accordance with VA regulations. The Contractor will provide VA staff access to VA Patient data and unique computerized interactive constructions via password protected Internet access. Access to any individual patient�s interactive model will be limited to only those provider(s) who originally requested the service. The period of performance is expected to be from December 22, 2026, through December 21, 2031. title: HALE COULEE BROME HERBICIDE TREATMENT
description: REQUEST FOR QUOTE Hale Coulee Herbicide Application Bureau of Land Management (BLM) - Montana Lewiston District Office This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation #140L3726Q0175 is issued as a Request for Quotes (RFQ). This RFQ is being issued as a total set-aside for small business. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Description Quantity/Acre Unit of Issue Unit Price Total CLIN 0010 Hale Coulee Herbicide Treatment 167 Acre $ $ Description: The Department of the Interior (DOI), Bureau of Land Management (BLM) Montana, Lewiston District Office (LDO) has a requirement for vegetation management services to minimize the negative impacts of invasive brome species on native plant communities, wildlife habitats, and livestock grazing areas by applying herbicide on up to 167 acres of BLM managed public land. Reduction and/or removal of invasive annual bromes from plant communities reduces competition for available resources and increases the resilience of native plant species. The goal is to restore mid and short grass prairie ecosystems within treated areas by increasing biodiversity and enhancing resiliency on BLM managed public lands over time. Details of this requirement can be found in the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS) and project maps. NAICS: 115310 - Support Activities for Forestry-Fuels Management PSC: F006 � Natural Resources/ Conservation � Land Treatment Practices Period of Performance: August 15, 2027 � October 1, 2027 Location: The Hale Coulee Annual Brome Treatment project is located approximately 10 miles NE from Winnett, Montana and approximately 60 nautical miles from Lewistown Airport, also located in Lewistown. Please see attached maps for further details. ______________________________________________________________________________ The BLM intends to award a firm fixed-price contract resulting from this RFQ using the lowest price technically acceptable (LPTA) source selection method. In order to be considered technically acceptable, the vendor must demonstrate technical capability and capacity to complete the required work in accordance with the PWS and have satisfactory past performance. In accordance with FAR Part 12 (RFO), offerors must include the following information with your quote submission: 1. Technical Capability (Ability to meet the specifications in the SOW - no longer than 5 pages). 2. Relevant Experience (2 projects ongoing or completed in the past 5 years) 3. Pricing Note: Any contractor submitting a quote must be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) at the time of submission and potential award. Please include your UEI and CAGE code with your submission. ______________________________________________________________________________ Please submit any questions via email to the Contract Specialist for this action, David Farina, no later than September 3, 2026 @ 2:30 PM MDT. The deadline for quote submission shall be Friday, September 11, 2026 @ 2:30 PM MDT. Quotes received after the deadline will not be considered. All quotes shall be submitted via email to David_farina@ios.doi.gov. Attachments: 1. Performance Work Statement, 17 pages 2. Hale Coulee Vicinity Map, 1 Page 3. Hale Coulee Unit Map, 1 Page 4. BLM Approved Adjuvants, 9 pages 5. BLM Herbicide Formulations, 20 pages 6. BLM Programmatic Approval ROD for Herbicide Treatments 7. Wage Determination 1976-1342, Rev 84, 3 Pages 8. Clauses and Provisions, 5 Pages

The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. Please see attached complete Sources Sought Notice and Draft PWS.
